theme: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

reports.title: Shaun Elliott
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

concerns.quote: Extensive areas of the evidence concerned a detailed examination of the Police missing person enquiry and the policies, protocols and resources relating to such enquiries. The policies adopted by Thames Valley Police largely follow national guidelines and the matters raised therefore go to that policy making. | am informed that the College is currently rewriting the NPIA Missing Person Guidance to be replaced by an Approved Professional Practice
concerns.hazard: Police missing person enquiry policies and resources

concerns.quote: The evidence revealed that a missing person coordinator was in post but not on duty at weekends. It was apparent from the evidence that an appropriately experienced coordinator will have the time and know-how to examine cases in fine detail. The officers directly responsible for the enquiry may have many other calls on their time. The IPCC report recommended there be cover 7 days a week. A senior police officer reported that this was under review and that other police forces were being contacted

Family Liaison. Shaun's family expressed a number of concerns and frustrations in this regard. However relevant to this report specific benefits could be derived from effective family liaison. Namely the family as a source of information together with the potential information sharing and cross referencing

reports.title: Alan Hirst: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: PolSAs are crucial to high risk missing person enquires. The inability of police forces to provide 24/7 365 day coverage of PolSA responsibilities is being impeded by: (1) insufficient provision of training places, and (2) the number of training places made available does not appear to prioritise those forces in most urgent need of PolSAs or those that cannot fulfil 24/7 365 day coverage.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of round‑the‑clock staffing for missing‑person investigation roles. The earlier report notes a missing‑person coordinator absent on weekends; the later report notes insufficient 24/7 coverage of PolSA duties due to training shortages.
